descriptionChirho: Nifal passive: to be shaken, moved, or disturbed from a stable position, often used of the earth, mountains, or the righteous who will not be moved.
Qal active and Hitpael: to totter, waver, or stagger physically, describing unsteady motion of a person or thing losing balance or stability.
Qal: to slip or lose one's footing, emphasizing a sudden loss of traction rather than gradual wavering, often of the foot slipping.
Hifil causative: to make someone or something fall, to bring down or topple, the causative counterpart of the basic totter/fall meaning.
